subject: Lion Family
fact: Lion cubs grow up in social groups called prides.

subject: Elephant Family
fact: Elephant calves stay close to their mothers and other herd members.

subject: Giraffe Family
fact: Newborn giraffe calves can stand and walk soon after birth.

subject: Zebra Family
fact: Zebra foals learn their mother's stripe pattern and scent.

subject: Gorilla Family
fact: Young gorillas ride on their mothers as they travel.

subject: Chimpanzee Family
fact: Chimpanzee youngsters spend years learning from their mothers.

subject: Orangutan Family
fact: Orangutan babies stay with their mothers for many years.

subject: Tiger Family
fact: Tiger cubs learn hunting skills from their mothers.

subject: Cheetah Family
fact: Cheetah cubs stay with their mother while learning to hunt.

subject: Leopard Family
fact: Leopard cubs are born with spotted coats.

subject: Wolf Family
fact: Wolf pups are raised by a family group called a pack.

subject: Fox Family
fact: Fox kits often play together near their den.

subject: Bear Family
fact: Bear cubs stay with their mother while learning where to find food.

subject: Polar Bear Family
fact: Polar bear cubs are born in snow dens and remain with their mother.

subject: Panda Family
fact: Giant panda cubs are tiny compared with their mothers at birth.

subject: Kangaroo Family
fact: A baby kangaroo is called a joey and develops inside its mother's pouch.

subject: Koala Family
fact: Koala joeys ride on their mother's back after leaving the pouch.

subject: Wombat Family
fact: Wombat joeys grow inside a backward-facing pouch.

subject: Wallaby Family
fact: Wallaby joeys develop in a pouch just like kangaroos.

subject: Meerkat Family
fact: Meerkat groups help watch over and protect young pups.

subject: Otter Family
fact: Otter pups learn to swim from their mothers.

subject: Beaver Family
fact: Young beavers called kits live with their family in a lodge.

subject: Raccoon Family
fact: Raccoon kits stay with their mother while learning to forage.

subject: Skunk Family
fact: Skunk kits follow their mother in a line while exploring.

subject: Deer Family
fact: A young deer is called a fawn and often has spots for camouflage.

subject: Moose Family
fact: Moose calves can walk soon after they are born.

subject: Bison Family
fact: Bison calves are sometimes called red dogs because of their reddish coats.

subject: Horse Family
fact: A baby horse is called a foal.

subject: Donkey Family
fact: A baby donkey is called a foal and stays close to its mother.

subject: Cow Family
fact: A baby cow is called a calf.

subject: Sheep Family
fact: A baby sheep is called a lamb.

subject: Goat Family
fact: A baby goat is called a kid.

subject: Pig Family
fact: A baby pig is called a piglet.

subject: Rabbit Family
fact: Baby rabbits are called kits or kittens.

subject: Dog Family
fact: Puppies are born with their eyes and ears closed.

subject: Cat Family
fact: Kittens depend on their mother for warmth and food when very young.

subject: Dolphin Family
fact: Dolphin calves swim beside their mothers and learn social skills.

subject: Orca Family
fact: Orca calves often stay with their mother's family group for life.

subject: Humpback Whale Family
fact: Humpback calves drink rich milk from their mothers.

subject: Manatee Family
fact: Manatee calves stay close to their mothers and learn where to feed.

subject: Seal Family
fact: Seal pups are born with coats suited to their cold or coastal habitats.

subject: Sea Lion Family
fact: Sea lion pups recognize their mothers by calls and smell.

subject: Walrus Family
fact: Walrus calves stay very close to their mothers in the water.

subject: Penguin Family
fact: Many penguin parents take turns caring for eggs and chicks.

subject: Emperor Penguin Family
fact: Emperor penguin fathers balance eggs on their feet during winter.

subject: Albatross Family
fact: Albatross parents may travel long distances to bring food back to their chicks.

subject: Owl Family
fact: Owlets stay in the nest while their parents bring food.

subject: Eagle Family
fact: Eaglets grow quickly and practice flapping before their first flight.

subject: Duck Family
fact: Ducklings can follow their mother soon after hatching.

subject: Goose Family
fact: Goslings can walk and swim shortly after hatching.

subject: Chicken Family
fact: Chicks communicate with their mother even before hatching.

subject: Crocodile Family
fact: Mother crocodiles may carry hatchlings gently in their mouths.

subject: Alligator Family
fact: Female alligators guard nests and help protect hatchlings.

subject: Sea Turtle Family
fact: Sea turtle hatchlings dig out of sandy nests and head toward the sea.

subject: Frog Family
fact: Frog eggs hatch into tadpoles before changing into frogs.

subject: Seahorse Family
fact: Male seahorses carry developing babies in a special pouch.

subject: Octopus Family
fact: Female octopuses guard their eggs until they hatch.

subject: Clownfish Family
fact: Clownfish parents clean and guard their eggs.

subject: Elephant Seal Family
fact: Elephant seal pups grow quickly by drinking rich milk.

subject: Prairie Dog Family
fact: Prairie dog pups live in underground family burrows called coteries.
